message.content:
### Logistic Regression – A Quick Overview | Topic | Details | |-------|---------| | **Purpose** | Predicts a binary outcome (e.g., yes/no, success/failure) based on one or more predictor variables. | | **Model Formulation** | Uses the *logit* link function:
$$\text{logit}(p)=\ln \frac{p}{1-p}=β_0+β_1x_1+\dots+β_kx_k$$
where \(p=P(Y=1|\mathbf{x})\). | | **Interpretation** | Coefficients (\(β_i\)) represent log‑odds changes per unit change in predictors. Exponentiating gives odds ratios. | | **Estimation Method** | Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE); iteratively reweighted least squares (IRLS) algorithm commonly used. | | **Assumptions** |
  • No perfect multicollinearity among predictors.
  • Linear relationship between continuous predictors and the logit of the outcome.
| | **Common Use Cases** | Medical diagnosis (disease vs. healthy), credit scoring (default vs. non-default), marketing (purchase vs. no purchase). | #### Why “Regression”? Although called regression, logistic regression models probabilities rather than continuous values. It's essentially a generalized linear model (GLM) with a binomial distribution and a logit link. --- If you’d like deeper dives—like regularization techniques (Lasso/L2), evaluation metrics (AUC‑ROC, confusion matrix), or implementation snippets—just let me know!
